messages.subject: Updates
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Google Summer of Code is now under way, and I would like to reiterate my
suggestion for some sort of common place on the web where we can informally
leave some progress notes -- be it weekly or bi-weekly.

Tal had set up the blog backend. Would any of our students like to start by
filling-in some content?

--
  Regards, Dirk

messages.subject: Re: Updates
messages.body_plain:
Re: rdax project (automatic differentiation in R), Chillu has been recording a progress
diary on my optimx wiki (currently login only) and we have been in contact with Tal about
the blog backend. The diary is mainly for us, so we both can see where we are at. However,
we've been discussing what material to put on the blog and also who to alert (outside of
GSoC folk) about what is happening, as a number of workers showed interest in AD and
several offered to provide advice etc.  I suspect several other projects are in a similar
situation -- some material, but not really enough to show off yet.

I also got Carol Smith's note about Welcome packages and note the matter of mid-term
evaluations. Perhaps Dirk or someone with previous experience would provide a note on the
process and timing for both mentors and students so we keep gsoc-r group in good standing.

Cheers, JN

messages.subject: Re: Updates
messages.body_plain:
I have been meaning to post about the progress in the ability for
automatic differentiation in R to a wider audience for quite some
time. Prof. John Nash and me already have in place, a system for
differentiation of non-singular univariate functions up to arbitrary
order, which is itself good news. However, I chose to wait to
implement a few more features before posting news about the progress
thus far. Specifically, I am currently working on multivariate
function differentiation which will conclude the development of the
forward mode of AD. My idea was that the completion of the forward
mode AD would be a logical milestone that would necessitate informing
the community at large.

However, I am sure that by the end of this week I will have a fully
functional package and a tutorial/demo that will demonstrate what can
be done using the AD engine. I am sorry for not having posted to the
blog (despite having supported the idea and saying that I would) and
keeping people in the dark about the project's progress.

The development of the package can be followed at:
http://github.com/quantumelixir/radx

Regards,
Chillu
